reason: The key premises are well-supported: E3 directly shows LCO changes with processing and raises dislocation barriers, E1 demonstrates that fault-energy fluctuations (not averages) govern strength, and E5 links heterogeneous strain fields to enhanced properties. E2 supports thermodynamic control of ordering. The cited evidence is accurately represented, with only minor overstatement in the quantitative 20–30% prediction, which is not directly attested in the passages.
premises: Lower-temperature annealing increases local chemical ordering (LCO) in single-phase FCC HEAs
Increased LCO enhances spatial fluctuations in local shear-fault energy
Enhanced shear-fault energy fluctuations create a more heterogeneous lattice strain field
This heterogeneity roughens dislocation slip pathways and increases dislocation pinning
Increased pinning raises yield strength and hardness by ~20–30%
